newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals except silver end firmer.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals except silver end firmer.

text.p: All yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures except silver ended firmer on Friday, buoyed by gains in bullion prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from one yen per gram lower to eight yen higher. Most-active benchmark February was up five yen at 1,378 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from seven yen to 19 yen per gram higher. Benchmark February was up 10 yen at 1,473 yen.
"Private investors were tending to buy gold while selling platinum due to a widening gold/platinum spread," one trader said.
In the spot gold market, bullion was a tad weaker, quoted at $342.00/342.30 per ounce in 0731 GMT, against $342.30/80 in New York on Thursday.
High platinum lease rates, reflecting a tightening in the spot market, supported platinum prices, the traders said.

Despite a planned visit by a Russian central bank mission with three Japanese trade houses on PGMs next week, lingering uncertainty over Russian metal supplies continued to lift platinum and palladium prices, the traders said.
Trade houses bought palladium futures, but private investors were generally sidelined amid uncertain direction.
Traders said trading in platinum group metal prices would continue to be volatile unless the Russian matter is settled.
Platinum prices ranged from seven yen to 19 yen per gram higher, with benchmark February up 10 yen at 1,473 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from two to 17 yen per gram up, with benchmark February up two yen at 594 yen.
Silver futures were weaker. Benchmark February was down 1.5 yen per 10 grams at 193.0 yen.
